title: The Part of Recovery Nobody Talks About

body.en: The water receded from Kojo's neighbourhood after five days. Everyone talked about the flood itself — the videos, the news coverage, the immediate rescue. Almost nobody talked about the eight months that came after: the mould that had to be cleared from every wall, the furniture that had to be replaced on no budget, the small business that took four months to reopen because the stock was ruined. Recovery isn't the dramatic part of a disaster. It's the slow, unglamorous part that determines whether a community actually gets back on its feet, or stays quietly worse off for years.

followUpQuestion: What part of recovery did Kojo's story say usually gets overlooked compared to the disaster itself?
